# Decision Log

This log covers the conversion of the 55 Mule 3 examples in this repository into standalone `<example>-java` Spring Boot projects. `sap-data-retrieval` is `EXCLUDED — pending sapjco3.jar`. Every non-trivial decision and every deviation from a literal reading of the request has a row. Rows D-001 … D-081 were set by the migration plan; rows from D-082 on record decisions taken while the projects were written. Rows are appended and never renumbered, and a row that supersedes or amends an earlier decision names that row.

Per-project status is in [SUMMARY.md](SUMMARY.md). The source-to-target mapping, whose Decision cells cite these IDs, is in [TRACEABILITY.md](TRACEABILITY.md).

| ID | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks / trade-offs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-001 | 56 folders exist, so 55 are delivered; General = 35; `SUMMARY.md` has 56 rows; the eventual total is 56 | Adopt the prompt's 57/36 figures | Folder listing and tech spec 1.2.3.3 show 56; no folder can be invented | Stakeholders expecting 57 rows see 56; `SUMMARY.md` header explains |
| D-002 | Projects are root-level siblings `<folder>-java`; not added to the root reactor; originals read-only | A `java/` subfolder; a new aggregator | Matches the prompt's naming; the root `pom.xml` is excluded from change; independence | Root listing doubles in length |
| D-003 | Naming: folder case preserved in project and artifactId; package lower-cased with `_`; PascalCase main class; subpackages `model`, `endpoint`, `listener`, `scheduler` and `client` added beside the five mandated ones | Put everything in the five packages | Keeps adapters and DTOs out of `controller` and `service` | Reviewers see extra packages |
| D-004 | Standalone projects: `spring-boot-starter-parent` only; cross-cutting classes duplicated per project | A shared library module or shared parent POM | "No shared cross-project runtime", independent `mvn clean install` | Fixes to shared patterns must be applied up to 55 times |
| D-005 | Spring Boot 3.2.12 | Another 3.2.x patch | Latest 3.2 patch on Central | BOM forces Jackson 2.15.4 onto `force-wsc` (declares 2.18.4); covered by Tier 2B |
| D-006 | `spring-ws.version` = 4.1.4 overrides the BOM's 4.0.11 | Keep 4.0.11 | Prompt pins 4.1.4; a scratch build on Boot 3.2.12/Framework 6.1.15 passed | 4.1.x is built against Framework 6.2; untested corners may surface |
| D-007 | Error bodies: original literal bodies preserved; `ErrorResponse{message, upstreamSystem}` only where the original has none | One uniform JSON error for everything | The contract requires the original payloads; the prompt's "consistent shape" is honoured for new cases | Two shapes coexist: literal original bodies and `ErrorResponse` for the connector failure modes; the RAML projects send no body where the RAML declares none |
| D-008 | rest-api-with-apikit `ConflictException` → bodyless 409 (no `Content-Type`) | Reproduce whatever the runtime returned; 409 with an `ErrorResponse` body | The RAML declares 409 without a body and governs RAML projects. The original runtime status is unverified: `ConflictException` extends APIkit's `MuleRestException` and no `apikit:mapping` handles it (0.3.3) | If the diagnostic capture of 0.7.2 shows another status, clients of the original saw a different status; a new DECISIONS row and the project README then record it (0.3.3) |

The M2M guides specify PS256 (0.3.6) | N+1 requests per search, disclosed in 0.10.5. The item quantity filter reads every supply plan (FB-NS-01). The project is reported `BLOCKED — pending approval of D-016` (0.7.4, 0.10.2) until the requester approves this deviation, and stays so while any FB-NS item is open under the closure rule of 0.6.5 |

| D-024 | Artemis replaces ActiveMQ 5. ActiveMQ's consumer-side `RedeliveryPolicy` becomes a listener-side `RedeliveryDelayPolicy`: first redelivery after 5000 ms, later ones after 2000 ms, at most 5 redeliveries (6 deliveries), as in [jms-message-rollback-and-redelivery/src/main/app/jms-redelivery.xml:6-11] | Broker-side `redelivery-delay` only; keep the ActiveMQ 5 client | The prompt pins the Artemis starter, and Artemis applies one broker-side delay, which cannot express the 5000/2000 pair (0.3.6) | The delay is held in the consumer, so a consumer restart during the wait redelivers sooner |

JAXB types are generated from the WSDLs, except in xml-only, which has DOM endpoints, and for `IProcessOrder`, whose ported model classes define the authored schema (D-076); no standalone XSD is hand-authored | Keep JAX-WS; hand-authored XSDs | JAX-WS is forbidden, and Spring WS is contract-first | Code-first WSDLs must match CXF's wire format; `WsdlContractTest` and the SoapUI envelopes are the reference |

Reader: the first attachment's bytes are decoded as UTF-8 and parsed with commons-csv 1.14.1 `CSVFormat.DEFAULT` set to take the header from the first record and skip it, with `,` separator, `"` quote and `\` escape, empty lines ignored and values neither trimmed nor stripped of surrounding spaces; LF, CRLF and CR all end a record; the format is built with `CSVFormat.Builder.get()`, which returns the same format as the deprecated `Builder.build()`; header names match case-sensitively, other columns are ignored and the header's column order does not change the output order. Layout: the declaration `<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>` (single quotes), LF line feeds, two spaces of indentation per level and no trailing line feed; `orders` holds one `order` per data record with `orderId`, `name`, `units`, `pricePerUnit` in that order; input with no data record (zero bytes, a header only, or only empty lines) gives `<orders/>`. Field forms: a column the header lacks, or a cell missing from a record shorter than the header, gives `<x/>`; an empty cell gives `<x></x>`; any other value is written unchanged as text (`2.0` stays `2.0`) with Woodstox's escaping: `&` → `&amp;`, `<` → `&lt;`, `>` → `&gt;` only at the start of a value or after `]`, CR → `&#xd;`, quotes and tabs unchanged. Errors propagate unchecked to the poller, which logs them (0.6.2): `UncheckedIOException` for malformed CSV such as an unterminated quoted value, `IllegalArgumentException` for a header with an empty column name, `IllegalStateException` for a character XML 1.0 forbids. DW 1.0 writes a null value (what `$.pricePerUnit` yields for a column the row lacks) as an inline-closed empty element, writes a string, the empty one included, between start and end tags, and writes an object with no fields (`orders: {}` after `payload map` over no rows) as an empty element; null handling follows the DW 1.0 writer (0.6.1), and the forms match DW-04's (D-113). The DataWeave CSV reader's documented defaults are `,` separator, `"` quote, `\` escape, a header row and empty lines ignored, and it represents every value as a string (D-177). The flow sets no encoding, and Mule 3's default `mule.encoding` is UTF-8. The `>` and CR escapes are Woodstox's and undocumented for DW 1.0. The IMAP twin writes an empty cell as `<x/>` and this mapper as `<x></x>`, so the two projects differ for that input until the captures settle it. MULE-8927 (fixed in Mule 3.8.0) changed how Mule treats `@` in email endpoint user and password attributes; how the 3.8 original treats an encoded or a malformed value has not been observed |

An array at the root or inside an array writes each item's content directly into the enclosing element, a scalar root becomes the text of `OrderTshirt` and a `null` root leaves it empty. For DW-37 and DW-38: unmarshalling to the generated types and writing them with Jackson's `ObjectMapper`, which gives typed numbers and schema order; `""` for an empty element, as D-194 reads DW-33's `<orderItems/>`; trimmed text; JSON arrays for repeated siblings, DataWeave's `duplicateKeyAsArray`. DW-35 and DW-37 only change the format (`ns0#OrderTshirt: payload`, `payload`), so the output carries the input's own members. The DataWeave 1.2 (Mule 3.9) format reference [mulesoft/docs-dataweave branch `v1.2`, `modules/ROOT/pages/dataweave-formats.adoc`] states that the XML model supports repeated keys (:328), that the XML reader reads a tag with empty or blank text as null by default (`nullValueOn` `empty`, :362), that the XML writer skips null values only under `skipNullOn` (:413,450-457), which DW-35 does not set, that the JSON writer indents by default (:517) and that repeated keys become an array only under `duplicateKeyAsArray`, default `false` (:522). An unprefixed DataWeave key has no namespace, so `ns0#` qualifies the root alone; XML text carries no number type, so every leaf is a string; `payload.ns0#ListInventoryResponse` selects only that qualified element. The streaming parser keeps member order, duplicate names and number text, while the tree model keeps one value per name and re-renders numbers, and the JAXB types impose the schema's members and order. The committed DW 1.0 output [processing-orders-with-dataweave-and-APIkit/src/main/resources/orders.json] uses two-space indentation, `": "` and no trailing line feed, while Jackson 2.15.4's default printer writes `" : "` (D-180). The reference describes DataWeave 1.2 on Mule 3.9, not the Mule 3.8 runtime. D-194 reads DW-33's empty `<orderItems/>` as `""`, so the two projects treat an empty element differently until a fixture settles it, and the reference's own example reads an empty element that carries attributes as `""` (:333-347), which this mapper writes as `null`. | D-348 | netsuite-data-retrieval-java's `mapper/NetsuiteValueMapper.enumeration` logs an unmapped `stage` or `creditHoldOverride` value at WARN as `Unmapped NetSuite enumeration value for <key>: <description>`, the description built by `describeEnumerationValue` [netsuite-data-retrieval-java/src/main/java/com/mulesoft/examples/netsuite_data_retrieval/mapper/NetsuiteValueMapper.java:116-120,357-507]. An object value is described as `object {id=<id>, refName=<refName>, <n> other members}`. `<id>` (`describeEnumerationId`) is a textual `id` in double quotes, a number or boolean one as its text, a missing one as `absent`, and any other one as its Jackson node type (`OBJECT`, `ARRAY`, `NULL`). `<refName>` (`describeEnumerationRefName`) carries none of the `refName`'s characters: a textual `refName` is `<redacted, <length> chars>` with its whole length in Java `char`s, e.g. `object {id="_partner", refName=<redacted, 7 chars>, 2 other members}`; a missing one is `absent`; any other one (JSON null, number, boolean, object, array) is its node type alone. `<n>` counts the remaining members, whose names and values are not logged. A textual value is described as `text "<text>"`, and any other value (number, boolean, array) as its node type alone. In every logged text (a textual `id` or a textual value) each ISO control character and each Unicode line or paragraph separator is replaced by `?`, and text longer than `LOGGED_TEXT_MAX` (64) characters is cut to 64 characters, or 63 where the cut would split a surrogate pair, and followed by `...(<length> chars)`. The key is still omitted, and the matching rules of D-294, which still compare the `refName` text, are unchanged | Log the whole `JsonNode`, the original behaviour; log the `refName` text bounded to 64 characters beside the `id`, the previous iteration of this row; log only the key; log a hash of the value; log the names of the object's members | FB-NS-04 requires the WARN to carry the REST value, and REST defines an enumeration value as `{id, refName}` [section_1545142146 "Format of Enumeration Values"]. The value itself is identified by `id`, which matching tries first, so the bounded `id` is logged. `refName` is a display label that may carry personal data, for example a person's name when an unexpected reference object arrives in the key, so only its length or type is logged (CWE-532). Any other member lies outside the enumeration format and can carry credentials or personal data, so only the count is logged. The key alone, or a hash, gives no value to compare with the candidates when FB-NS-04 is checked against live data, and member names would still disclose the shape of unexpected content. Replacing control and separator characters keeps one log line per event (CWE-117), and the length cap bounds each entry | An unknown value's other members are not visible for diagnosis, only their count. A `refName` mismatch is visible only by its length or type, so a candidate that differs from the label only in spelling cannot be read from the log. An `id` longer than 64 characters is truncated, and a replaced character cannot be told apart from a literal `?`. An `id` that itself carries sensitive text is still logged, within the cap |

## Adding rows

- A new row is appended to the end of the table above with the next free ID (the first execution-time row was D-082) and fills all five cells.
- The requester's approval of D-016, D-027, D-032 or D-078 is recorded as a new row. Only such a row changes the affected project's Delivery label from `BLOCKED — pending approval of <D-ID>` to `DELIVERED` (D-079). An approval of D-016 that accepts named FB-NS items as deviations lists those items in its row.
- These results are also recorded as new rows: each `volatile` regex of a Tier 2A fixture (0.7.2); the NetSuite field-coverage and SuiteQL name results (FB-NS-02, FB-NS-09); the status and body the RAML 409 diagnostic capture of rest-api-with-apikit observes (0.3.3, D-008); a revised Workday WSDL hash (D-078); and the exact version of a supplied `sapjco3.jar` patch (D-047).
- A project README and its `TRACEABILITY.md` section cite the ID of every row that concerns the project.
